bib.title: LIMO: Less is More for Reasoning

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; no appendix exists.

question: Can sophisticated mathematical reasoning be elicited by SFT on only a few hundred examples instead of tens of thousands?
hypothesis: In foundation models whose domain knowledge is comprehensively encoded in pretraining, minimal but strategically designed demonstrations of cognitive processes suffice to elicit complex reasoning (LIMO Hypothesis).
contributions: Construct the LIMO dataset (800 samples) and SFT Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, with strong in-domain and OOD results.
Ablations on chain quality, question difficulty, backbone knowledge, model size and data size.

method.summary: Filter millions of math questions to 2,125 hard ones (LIMO-Pool) by difficulty from model solve rates, pick the best of multiple R1-class solutions per question with a rule-based quality score, keep the top 800, and run full-parameter SFT on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct. Compare against SFT on NuminaMath-100k and OpenThoughts-114k and ablate quality, difficulty, backbone and size.
method.task: Mathematical reasoning with verifiable answers; SFT on long chain-of-thought

datasets.name: LIMO (800) / LIMO-Pool (2,125)
datasets.source: Pool from NuminaMath-CoT, DeepScaleR (~40,000 pairs), pre-2024 AIME, MATH, Chinese exams; solutions from DeepSeek R1, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, QwQ-32B
datasets.preprocessing: Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct filter (drop problems solved within 4 attempts); R1-Distill-Qwen-32B 32 samples, keep 1-3/32 solved; n-gram dedup against benchmarks; rule-based chain score (length 30%, check/verify words 20%, tentative words 25%, connectives 25%, normalized by text length)

datasets.name: OlympiadBench, CHMath, Gaokao, Kaoyan, GradeSchool, Minerva, GPQA
datasets.source: CHMath, Gaokao, Kaoyan new from 2024 exams; GradeSchool authors' own

models.name: LIMO
models.context: inferred: 16,384-token SFT sequence limit; 32,768 max output at eval

training.seq_len: 16,384 (limit; all SFT responses are under it)

other.note: Same recipe is said to be used for ablations and baselines; the paper does not say whether epochs were kept at 15 for the 100k datasets.

inference.decoding: greedy single sample for large benchmarks; sampling for AIME24, AMC23, CHMath
inference.samples: 4 samples per problem for benchmarks under 50 problems (AIME24, AMC23, CHMath), unbiased pass@1; 1 greedy sample otherwise

metrics.name: pass@1
metrics.definition: zero-shot CoT; unbiased pass@1 (Chen et al., 2021) on small sets; rule-based check for numeric answers, LLM-based evaluator for complex formats

eval.protocol: Single training run per configuration; no seeds, intervals or significance tests stated. LLM evaluator model not named.

evidence.quote: We set as our sequence length limit because all SFT response sequences remain under 16,384 tokens.

results.claim: LIMO reaches 63.3% on AIME24 from 800 examples, from base 16.5%.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct full-parameter SFT on 800 LIMO samples, 15 epochs, pass@1 zero-shot CoT, 32,768 max output tokens; AIME24 uses 4 samples at temperature 0.6, unbiased pass@1
results.quote: LIMO achieves 63.3% accuracy, outperforming QwQ-32B-Preview (50.0%) and OpenAI-o1-preview (44.6%)

results.setup: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct full-parameter SFT on 800 LIMO samples, 15 epochs, pass@1 zero-shot CoT, 32,768 max output tokens; greedy single sample
results.quote: LIMO achieves a notable 95.6% accuracy, surpassing QwQ-32B-Preview (89.8%) and OpenAI-o1-preview (85.5%)

results.claim: LIMO averages 78.1 across 10 benchmarks versus 58.3 for OpenThoughts-114k and 32.3 for NuminaMath-100k, all on the same backbone.
results.setup: Table 1, same Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct backbone; base model averages 49.9
results.quote: LIMO achieves the highest average performance of 78.1% across all benchmarks

results.claim: NuminaMath-100k SFT degrades the base model's average (32.3 vs 49.9).
results.setup: SFT of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on a random 100k subset of NuminaMath-CoT
results.quote: NuminaMath-100k shows significant degradation (32.3% vs. base model’s 49.9%) due to uncurated reasoning chains
results.note: Cause (uncurated chains) is asserted, not tested.

results.claim: Same 800 examples on Qwen1.5-32B-Chat give only 9.2% AIME24, 54.1 points below Qwen2.5.
results.setup: Qwen1.5-32B-Chat vs Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, identical LIMO SFT
results.quote: a 54.1 percentage point improvement over Qwen1.5’s 9.2%

results.claim: Advanced-500 (AIME) questions give AIME24 51.5%, and 91.2% MATH500 with no MATH data.
results.setup: 500 problems each of Simple (MATH 1-2), Complex (MATH 3-5), Advanced (AIME), R1-written solutions, SFT of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct
results.note: Text says '16% accuracy improvement' without naming the comparison set; read the values in Fig 4.

results.claim: 400 samples already lift AIME24 from 16.5 to 57.5.
results.setup: LIMO-400, top 400 by quality score from LIMO-pool
results.quote: increasing AIME24 accuracy from 16.5 to 57.5 and MATH500 accuracy from 79.4 to 94.8

results.claim: 2k samples give 69.6 on AIME24 and 95.8 on MATH500, with diminishing returns beyond 800.
results.quote: The highest dataset size (2k) provides the best overall performance (69.6 on AIME24, 95.8 on MATH500)

results.claim: 72B model gets 68.3 on AIME24 vs 63.3 for 32B; 3B gets 2.5.
results.quote: rising from 2.5 for the 3B model to 68.3 for the 72B model

results.claim: Reasoning-chain quality matters: L5 chains give highest AIME24/MATH500, decreasing with level.
results.setup: 500 questions, five quality levels L1-L5 from the rule-based score; values only in Fig 3

limits: Math only, on one backbone family (Qwen); smaller Qwen sizes show 3B gets 2.5 on AIME24, so the effect depends on the base model.
Authors concede the lower bound on samples is open.
Data selection used the AIME-style difficulty signal from R1-distill models, so the 800 depend on stronger teachers.
Single runs, no seeds or intervals; LLM judge unnamed; hardware, compute and optimizer not stated.

Baseline datasets differ in domain and curation, so the 'quality over quantity' reading is not isolated beyond the RQ1/RQ2 ablations; the NuminaMath and OpenThoughts failure causes are speculation ('probably due to').
Later work (cited in the repo notes) finds scale beats hand-curation for general reasoning; this paper does not test that.

terms.definition: In foundation models where domain knowledge has been comprehensively encoded during pre-training, sophisticated reasoning can emerge through minimal but strategically designed demonstrations of cognitive processes.
